summary: David Jonathan Ross's product page for Fit, an ultra-condensed-to-ultra-wide variable font (wdth 100–3600): almost every line on the page is fitted to the column width by a JavaScript 'var-to-width' routine, so the page itself is the demo. Trash-talk slogans, red/black/white statement walls, script extensions by guest designers, a language word wall, resizable 'TRY ME!' tester, Fonts In Use grid and DJR's standard on-page licence cart.

instances.look: Ten full-width lines on a charcoal gradient, alternating white and light grey, each a two-word insult to a classic typeface ('Dump Didot', 'Cut Caslon', 'Trash Times', 'Reject Rotis', 'Abandon Arial', 'Hurl Helvetica', 'Forsake Futura', 'Chuck Clarendon', 'Give up Garamond', 'Renounce Rockwell'), every line justified edge to edge by its own width value
instances.ux: Lines refit live when the window is resized (each line's wdth is recomputed); DJR site nav bar above
instances.learn: Write lines of different lengths and let the width axis justify each one to the same measure: the variable range becomes visible as rhythm

reconstruction.layout: ~3.9 screens; full-width column (1440 minus ~40px margins); 10 lines stacked with ~10px gaps, each ~330px tall; background linear gradient #2d2d2d → #141414
reconstruction.typography: Fit Variable at ~432px, per-line 'wdth' between ~368 and ~557 (computed), 'hght' 0; mixed case with a small-cap 'p' in 'Dump' (ss13 elsewhere); colours alternate #ffffff / #dfdfdf
reconstruction.behaviour: var-to-width script: on load/resize each figure.var-to-width binary-searches the wdth value so the span fills its container (data-width-readout stores the value)
reconstruction.content: 'Dump Didot / Cut Caslon / Trash Times …' — verbs of rejection + famous typeface names

instances.look: Thin black DJR site bar above the hero (not cut as a block): 'DAVID JONATHAN ROSS' left; FONTS, CLUB, TYPESET, GLYPHS, NOTES, ABOUT, Sign in, Cart right
instances.ux: Static site navigation; mobile collapses to MENU
instances.learn: A foundry-wide bar keeps the product page part of the catalogue

reconstruction.layout: Full-width bar ~33px tall at the top of the page
reconstruction.typography: ~11px Input Sans Narrow caps, tracked, white on black

instances.look: Title lockup inside a thin red frame on white: 'FIT' in huge black at a very wide setting over 'IS ALL YOU NEED!' in red condensed caps, with small red TRY · BUY · TYPESET · PDF buttons centred below
instances.ux: Drag the frame's left or right handle and both lines refit their width live; TRY adds a free testing licence to the cart, BUY jumps to the cart section, TYPESET opens typeset.djr.com, PDF downloads the specimen
instances.learn: Give the visitor the container, not the slider: resizing a frame shows what a width axis is for

reconstruction.layout: Frame ~1420×1060px with 1px red border and square handles on the east/west edges; 'FIT' fills ~65% of the height, the red line the rest; buttons row ~50px below
reconstruction.typography: 'FIT' ~864px Fit Variable wdth ~1009 with ss13; second line uppercase wdth ~401, red #cc090a; buttons ~11px Input Sans caps white on red
reconstruction.behaviour: Pointer drag on .handle-e / .handle-w changes .resize-box width → var-to-width recomputes wdth for each figure
reconstruction.html: div.resize-box > figure.var-to-width.big.no-resize + figure.var-to-width.red-hilite + .handle.handle-e/.handle-w; .try-buy-pdf form posting a Testing licence to commerce/cart/update-cart

instances.look: Three statement walls, every line justified by width: on red, 'Fit is designed to fit / Just about any text / Into just about any space' in white; on red, 'Difficult to read / BUT / Impossible to miss!' with a huge wide 'BUT'; on white, 'FIT IS THE SHIT!' in red caps over 'Grab a license now' in black
instances.ux: Lines refit when the window resizes
instances.learn: Admit the font's weakness in display size ('Difficult to read BUT impossible to miss'): honesty set at full width is the strongest pitch

reconstruction.layout: Each wall ~1.3 screens, lines full width with ~10px gaps; red sections use a vertical gradient #c90202 → #9b0101
